summary.prose: This Epic makes the in-editor dev-chat read and behave like the terminal-style agent surface it imitates. Tool activity becomes legible at a glance (the command, then its output, with long output collapsed to a short preview you can expand), the agent's own responses get the width and full-height treatment they deserve, the input reads as a real terminal prompt, permission cards settle into a clear approved/rejected state without leaving a confusing extra line in the transcript, and the agent can offer the user concrete choices to pick from when it needs direction. The result is a panel that is easier to follow, audit, and steer.

body.problem: The dev-chat panel is usable but its transcript and input do not read the way a developer expects a terminal-style agent chat to read, which erodes trust in what the agent is doing. Tool activity is the worst offender: the result of a tool the agent ran is frequently not shown at all, and when it is shown it fills the transcript at full height, so a reader cannot quickly see what command ran versus what it returned, and long outputs bury the surrounding conversation. The agent's own prose, by contrast, is cramped into a narrow column that leaves large empty space, making the primary content harder to read than the noise around it. The message box does not read as a terminal prompt and its prompt glyph is inert, so the surface feels unlike the tool it is imitating. The permission gate is confusing after the fact: once a request is approved or rejected its action buttons remain live and clickable, and an approval additionally drops a synthesized instruction line into the transcript as if the user had typed it, so the record of what happened around a permission decision is ambiguous. Finally, when the agent needs the user to choose between options to proceed, there is no way to present those choices — the user must infer them from prose and reply free-form, which is slow and error-prone. Together these gaps make the panel feel unfinished and make it harder to follow, audit, and steer an agent run.

nonGoals.text: Releasing the updated extension to the VS Code Marketplace.
nonGoals.rationale: Publishing is a separate, manual release step tracked elsewhere; this Epic delivers the behaviour behind the existing feature flag, not a store release.

nonGoals.text: Adding a real in-turn permission-grant channel for the claude provider (the deferred 'FIX #2').
nonGoals.rationale: The shipped Approve bugfix already conveys grants via a resume turn; a native in-turn control_response path is a distinct, larger change and is out of scope for this UX Epic.

nonGoals.text: Changing the underlying provider CLIs, their permission model, or which tools the agent may run.
nonGoals.rationale: This Epic is presentation and interaction polish over the existing event stream; the agent's capabilities and the sandbox/permission semantics are unchanged.

nonGoals.text: Reworking the durable transcript/session storage format or migrating existing sessions.
nonGoals.rationale: New behaviours must be additive and absent-safe over the existing stored shape; a storage migration is explicitly excluded to keep the Epic low-risk.

assumptions.text: The webview render layer is a single eval'd source module consumed only by the host panel, so render changes have a contained blast radius.
The event stream has no tool-output/result kind and no user-choice/selection kind today, so surfacing tool output and offering choices each require a new event flowing end to end.

The approval gate's request is live-only (never persisted) and an approval currently produces a visible synthesized user turn, so the resolved-state and outcome display are render/host concerns layered on the existing shipped grant behaviour.

constraints.text: Every new event and every new webview<->host message MUST be additive: the existing event kinds and protocol messages keep their shape and behaviour, and consumers that ignore the new fields are unaffected.

Any newly persisted row kind MUST have an explicit persistence mapping in the marker mapper; ephemeral, live-only surfaces (like the permission request and any transient choice prompt) MUST NOT leak into the durable replayable transcript.
Webview host/render behaviour is verified through the established eval'd *WebviewSource test pattern; new render branches and interactions must be covered that way.

The permission-decision OUTCOME display must preserve the shipped Approve behaviour (the underlying resume turn that actually conveys the grant); only the VISIBLE transcript echo of that grant may change.
All changes ship behind the existing insrc.chat.enabled flag (default off) and stay within the dev-chat module; no other plugin surface is affected.

stories.title: Make tool output legible: command, separator, output, collapsed by default
stories.userValue: As a developer watching an agent run, I can always see what a tool did — the command it ran and what it returned — without long output burying the conversation, so I can follow and audit the run at a glance.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the agent runs a tool that produces output
acceptanceCriteria.when: the turn renders in the transcript
acceptanceCriteria.then: a tool entry is shown containing the command that ran, a visual separator, and the output

acceptanceCriteria.given: a tool entry whose output is longer than a few lines
acceptanceCriteria.then: the output is collapsed to a short preview (about three lines) and can be expanded to full length and collapsed again on demand
it is shown in full and is never collapsed

acceptanceCriteria.when: the session is reloaded and the transcript replays
acceptanceCriteria.then: each tool entry restores with the same command/separator/output structure and its default-collapsed output state

localConstraints.text: Surfacing tool output must be additive to the existing event stream — no existing event kind changes shape, and turns without tool output render as before.

functionalRequirements.statement: Every tool the agent runs shows its result in the transcript as the command, a separator, then the output.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Tool output is currently often missing; when present it is unstructured.

functionalRequirements.statement: Tool output is collapsed to a short preview by default and can be expanded and re-collapsed.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Long output must not bury the surrounding conversation.
The collapse behaviour is scoped strictly to tool output; primary content always shows in full.

stories.title: Terminal-style input with a send prompt, and full-width assistant output
stories.userValue: As a user of the dev-chat, the input reads like a real terminal prompt I can send from directly, and the agent's responses use the width of the panel, so the surface feels like the terminal-style tool it imitates and is easy to read.

acceptanceCriteria.then: it reads as a terminal prompt with a leading prompt indicator

acceptanceCriteria.when: the user activates the leading prompt indicator
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message is sent, identically to the existing send action
it spans the large majority (about 90%) of the panel width rather than a narrow column

localConstraints.text: Input and layout changes are presentation-only; the send intent and the message it produces are unchanged.

functionalRequirements.statement: The message input reads as a terminal prompt whose leading indicator sends the message.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Aligns the surface with the terminal-style chat and removes the inert prompt glyph.

functionalRequirements.statement: Assistant text output uses about 90% of the panel width.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Removes wasted right-side space and makes the primary content easier to read.

stories.title: Resolved permission card shows its outcome without a synthesized turn
stories.userValue: As a user answering a permission prompt, once I approve or reject it the card clearly shows the outcome and stops offering buttons, and no confusing extra line is added as if I had typed it, so the record around a permission decision is unambiguous.

acceptanceCriteria.when: the user approves or rejects it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the card shows the decided outcome (approved or rejected) and no longer offers approve/reject actions

acceptanceCriteria.given: a permission request that is approved
acceptanceCriteria.then: no separate synthesized instruction line appears in the transcript as if typed by the user

acceptanceCriteria.given: a permission request that is approved
acceptanceCriteria.then: the underlying grant still takes effect and the run proceeds exactly as it does today
the card does not reappear as an actionable pending request

localConstraints.text: The resolved-outcome display must not alter the shipped grant behaviour: approval still conveys the grant via the underlying resume turn; only the visible transcript echo of that grant changes.

functionalRequirements.statement: A permission card settles into a decided (approved/rejected) state after the user acts, with its action buttons removed.
functionalRequirements.rationale: A resolved gate must be unambiguous and not leave live buttons.

functionalRequirements.statement: An approval no longer adds a visible synthesized instruction line to the transcript, while still granting as before.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Removes the confusing extra turn without changing what actually happens.

stories.title: Agent can present selectable options for the user to choose
stories.userValue: As a user, when the agent needs me to choose between options to proceed, I can pick from selectable choices directly instead of guessing and typing a free-form reply, so steering the agent at a decision point is fast and unambiguous.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the agent needs the user to choose among options to proceed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user sees the options as directly selectable controls, supporting either a single choice or multiple choices

acceptanceCriteria.when: the user makes a selection and confirms it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run continues based on the user's selection
a resolved prompt shows the chosen option(s) and an unresolved live prompt does not reappear as an actionable, durable transcript row

localConstraints.text: The selection round-trip must be additive to the event stream and the webview<->host protocol; existing message flows are unchanged and a turn without a choice prompt behaves as before.

functionalRequirements.statement: The agent can present the user a set of options for direct selection (single or multiple).
functionalRequirements.rationale: Replaces slow, error-prone free-form replies at choice points.

functionalRequirements.statement: The user's selection is conveyed back and the run continues based on it.
functionalRequirements.rationale: The choice must actually steer the run.
